title: Cozonac
subtitle: Romanian sweet enriched bread
excerpt: A pillowy, enriched loaf made with eggs, butter, and lemon zest, brushed with honey and baked until deeply golden. Cozonac is Romania's festive sweet bread, made at Christmas and Easter. The process takes a few hours but is straightforward and the result is deeply rewarding.
sourceNotes: Cozonac is Romania's festive sweet bread. It is made at Christmas and Easter. The dough is enriched with eggs and butter, then shaped and baked into a pillowy, fragrant loaf. It is a long process but the result is deeply rewarding.

content.text: Cozonac uses baking powder rather than yeast, so the rise comes entirely from the leavening and the kneading. Knead for a full 10 minutes -- the dough should feel smooth and slightly springy. The honey brushed over the top before baking gives it a deep golden crust.
Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar in a large bowl. Make a well in the centre.
Add eggs, warm milk, softened butter, vanilla, and lemon zest. Mix then knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Shape into a ball. Cover with a clean cloth and leave in a warm place for 1 hour.
Punch the dough down. Roll out into a rectangle about 30x40cm. Roll up tightly into a log. Place seam-side down in a greased 900g loaf tin. Cover and rest for 45 minutes.
Brush the top generously with honey. Bake at 175°C for 40-45 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding when tapped on the base.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes then transfer to a rack.

items.symptom: Bread is dense and doesn't rise
items.cause: Milk too hot or leavening inactive
items.fix: Warm milk should be hand-warm, not hot. Check baking powder is fresh.

content.text: Romania and Moldova. Made in every Romanian home at Christmas. Bakeries compete on whose cozonac is softest. Often given as a gift, beautifully wrapped and tied with ribbon.
